findings.F1: The book's falls come from shorts held into sharp relief rallies. In folds B and C the chained book's deepest fall is -8.1 % (w9), and its 10 worst days, from -4.9 % to -1.1 %, all fall on days the coins rose by +2.1 % to +14.9 %; the 5 % worst held case loses -6.7 % in one day.
findings.F2: The effect lives entirely in the 5-day fall, and the one-day fade is graded by it. On held cases the next-day short return is +3.16 % (t 5.68, n 99) when the 5-day return is below -2.1 daily swings, +1.26 % (t 2.17) between -2.1 and -0.85, +0.69 % (t 1.50) between -0.85 and +0.07, and -0.19 % (t -0.49, n 99) when the 5-day return is above +0.07 swings.
findings.F3: The deep 5-day fall is not an effect of its own. In falling markets, bars with a 5-day return below -2.1 swings and no run-ending up day give a next-day short return of -0.32 % (t -1.04, n 366), against +3.60 % (t 5.41, n 71) when the run-ending up day is there too. On all falling-market bars the next-day short return is +0.01 % (t 0.09, n 2063), so the 5-day fall belongs to the idea's trapped-holder situation.
findings.F4: The run-length part adds size without adding edge. The short return is not graded by run length (run 2: +1.65 %, run 3: +0.03 %, run 4: +1.36 %, run 5+: +2.28 %). The forecast bucket from -12.3 to -10, where the 5-day part is mostly clipped to 0 and only the run's fall sizes the short, earns +0.03 % (t 0.10, n 169), against +2.52 % (t 5.03) in the deepest bucket.
findings.F5: Keeping only the deep-5-day-fall cases cuts the falls by more than it cuts the gain. A rebuilt book on folds B and C holding the same shorts only when the 5-day return is below -0.85 swings keeps 197 of 394 cases. It has a yearly +17.3 % and a deepest fall of -4.5 % (Calmar 3.84), against +17.9 % and -7.6 % (Calmar 2.37) as held. Cutting only the cases with a 5-day rise gives Calmar 2.89 (fall -6.4 %).
findings.F6: A longer horizon adds nothing. The 2-day short return on deep-5-day-fall signals is +3.49 %, against +3.60 % over 1 day, so the move is spent in the next day.
findings.F7: The idea's size covers its cost. The unusual move is +0.91 % per case (t 3.49, 423 days), 4.7 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade, and it rises to about +3.6 % in the deepest 5-day-fall cases (F2). The book's failure (Calmar 0.55) is one of falls taken on the weak cases, not of cost.

ideas.idea: In a falling market, the first up day after a run of consecutive down days is followed by a fall in the coin's close over the next day, only while the coin's 5-day return is still a fall. That fall is larger the deeper the coin's 5-day fall, measured against its usual daily swing over the last 30 days, whatever the run's own length.
ideas.consequence: A trader fades a relief day only after the coin has just been sold hard over five days, sized by that fall. He stays out when the five days are flat or up, where the shorts meet the squeezes that make the book's deepest falls.
ideas.name: five-day-fall graded relief fade
